summary: Census: every piece of intelligence the pipeline computes vs whether the dashboard tells it as a story

items.intelligence: objective — the deduced Meta campaign objective (e.g. OUTCOME_SALES for rawafrican, OUTCOME_LEADS for NTI)
items.gap: Both cards map the raw enum through a bilingual label dict (مبيعات Sales / عملاء محتملون Leads). This is the one field told as a plain-language answer. Minor: no one-line 'what this means for you' subtitle, but the label is human.

items.intelligence: destination — the concrete conversion surface the objective drives to (online_store, lead_form)
items.gap: Mapped to Arabic labels (المتجر الإلكتروني / نموذج تسجيل). Told fine. The owner is not told this was CHOSEN from the surfaces the scrape actually found (the grounding story behind it stays hidden).

items.intelligence: funnel_stage — where this objective sits in the customer journey (bofu)
items.gap: The STUDIO card prints the raw uppercased enum 'BOFU' (server.py:564) — pure media-buyer jargon a business owner cannot read. The export maps it to 'تحويل · BOFU' but still leans on the acronym. Needs 'ready-to-buy customers' framing, not BOFU.

items.intelligence: rationale — the one-sentence grounded reason for this objective+destination
items.gap: This is the closest thing to a story sentence and both cards show it. Truncated at 220 chars. It is the ONLY 'why' the owner gets — everything supporting it (evidence quote, alternatives, confidence) is stripped, so the sentence stands alone without its proof.

items.intelligence: budget_allocation_pct — this objective's share of the plan budget
items.gap: The studio card shows 'الميزانية 100%' — vacuous, since every real plan is single-objective and auto-resolves to 100 (schemas.py:263). It reads like a real budget figure but carries zero information. There is NO absolute budget amount and NO cross-channel split. A paying owner asking 'how much do I spend and where?' gets a hollow 100%.

items.intelligence: channel_weights — per-channel budget emphasis (FB/IG/TikTok/YT) computed by category class
items.gap: The pipeline computes a real category-tuned split (e.g. clinic = FB 0.50 / IG 0.30 / YT 0.15) but it is NEVER attached to the MediaPlan nor rendered anywhere. This is exactly the 'where do I put my money' story the owner is paying for, and it is dead code from the dashboard's view.

items.intelligence: num_ad_sets — how many ad sets sit under the objective (drives the learning floor)
items.gap: Never shown. Fine to hide from a lay owner, but it means the whole learning-floor safeguard (below) is invisible — the owner has no sense of how the plan will be structured into testable units.

items.intelligence: test_budget + the 3×CPL learning-floor guardrail (min spend to read a result)
items.gap: test_budget is null in both artifacts and never rendered; the learning-floor logic (don't judge an ad before ~3 conversions of spend) is a genuinely useful 'don't panic on day 1' story completely absent from the dashboard. The owner sees no testing budget and no guidance on how long to let it run.

items.intelligence: audience_refinement — per-objective widen/narrow over the base persona (TOFU widen / BOFU narrow)
items.gap: null in current single-objective artifacts and never rendered. Not a live gap today, but the field designed to carry 'for this stage, target THESE people specifically' has no home on the dashboard.

items.intelligence: kpi_target.metric — the metric the campaign optimises (cost_per_purchase, cost_per_lead)
items.computed_where: media_plan/schemas.py:126 + config.py:64 default_kpi; rendered build.py:418 + server.py:566
items.gap: Both cards print the raw snake_case key verbatim — 'cost_per_purchase' / 'cost_per_lead'. That is a database field name, not language. Needs 'Cost per sale' / 'Cost per enquiry' and a note that this is the number we'll watch.

items.intelligence: kpi_target.target_value — the numeric goal for the metric (honest-unknown: null at plan time)
items.gap: Always null (honestly TBD until launch data exists), and the dashboard shows NOTHING where a target should be — no number, and crucially no honest 'we'll calibrate this after your first ~50 conversions' message. config.py's docstring claims the dashboard 'surfaces them as editable' but there is NO editable KPI UI anywhere. The owner is left not knowing whether a target is missing or just hidden.

items.intelligence: kpi_target.unit + window_days — the currency (EGP) and measurement window (7 days)
items.gap: Neither the unit nor the 7-day window is rendered. Even with no target number, telling the owner 'measured over the first 7 days, in EGP' would frame expectations. Both are dropped.

items.intelligence: confidence — how sure the deduction engine is about this objective (both artifacts = 'high')
items.gap: The engine computes and stores confidence='high' and it is never shown. A paid client deliverable that says 'we're highly confident in this recommendation' vs 'this is a tentative guess' materially changes trust — that signal is thrown away.

items.intelligence: alternatives — the objectives considered-but-rejected, in order (rawafrican: Traffic, Leads, Awareness)
items.gap: The single richest 'why this and not that' story — the engine records the runner-up objectives — and it is completely dropped. An owner (or the sales defense) wants 'we chose Sales over Traffic because you have a real checkout'. That narrative is computed and discarded.

items.intelligence: evidence[] — the resolved claim + verbatim quote proving the objective is grounded (e.g. 'Twice A week Oiling Routine — Sale price LE 440.00')
items.computed_where: media_plan/schemas.py:214 CampaignObjective.evidence (EvidenceRef claim/quote/resolved); reduced build.py:389-391 + server.py:541-545
items.gap: The whole evidence chain is collapsed into a single checkmark badge — 'مؤكد بالأدلة ✓' vs 'للمراجعة ⚠'. The actual proof quote (the real price line, the contact-form finding) is never shown. The moat of this product is 'grounded, here's the receipt' — the receipt is hidden and the owner just sees a green tick with no way to see WHAT was verified.

items.intelligence: base_persona.interests — the audience the brand talks to (claim: 'the brand's audience: B2C' / 'mixed')
items.gap: The export prints the internal claim string verbatim — 'the brand's audience: B2C' — engine-internal phrasing, not a sentence. Worse, the studio card renders NO persona at all (server.py has zero persona code). The rich evidence quotes behind it ('Loved by 17k+ Customers') are also dropped. The owner never gets a human 'who we're targeting and why' paragraph.

items.intelligence: base_persona.age_range + gender — demographic axes of the target audience
items.computed_where: media_plan/schemas.py:140-141; build.py:400-405 (rendered if present) / server.py none
items.gap: Null in both real artifacts (the pipeline didn't evidence them), so nothing shows — but that itself is the gap: an audience with no age or gender is barely an audience to a business owner, and the dashboard neither fills it nor flags 'age/gender not yet determined'. The studio card wouldn't render them even if present.

items.intelligence: base_persona.income_level — the audience's income tier
items.gap: Null in both artifacts and not in either card's render path (build.py:400 loops only age_range/gender/interests). Even if the engine populated it, there is no place for it to appear.

items.intelligence: base_persona.location_summary — evidenced summary of where the audience is
items.computed_where: media_plan/schemas.py:144; artifact value present but resolved=false
items.gap: The axis is not in any render path, AND in both real artifacts it is ungrounded (resolved:false) with a raw serialized dict dumped into the claim string ('serves: [{value: Egypt, evidence:...'). So it is both un-surfaced and, underneath, a broken data-quality value — an owner would see nothing, which at least hides the mess but loses the 'your customers are in Egypt' story.

items.intelligence: base_geo.mode — the geographic targeting strategy (national vs radius)
items.gap: Both cards translate the mode to a phrase ('قومي — كل البلد' / national). Told acceptably. Both real artifacts fell back to NATIONAL because the address axis went ungrounded — the owner isn't told WHY it's nationwide vs local.

items.intelligence: base_geo.center_address + radius_km — the local targeting anchor and its radius
items.gap: When a radius plan exists both cards show 'address · N km'. Fine when present, but both current artifacts are national so this never fires — and NTI/rawafrican DO have real addresses (Smart Village, Mall of Arabia) that failed to promote to a radius, so the owner loses a legitimate local-targeting recommendation.

items.intelligence: base_geo.cities + regions — explicit city/governorate target lists
items.gap: Empty in both artifacts and never rendered. No render path exists even if the CITIES/REGIONS modes were used, so an entire class of geo recommendation ('run in Cairo + Alexandria') can never reach the owner.

items.intelligence: base_geo.address_ref — the evidence grounding the geo anchor in the brand's real address
items.gap: Null in both artifacts and never surfaced. The grounding link that would let the owner trust 'we're targeting around YOUR branch' is absent.

items.intelligence: market_definition_ref — link to the competitor MarketDefinition the plan was built against
items.gap: Never rendered. Low priority for a lay owner, but it means the plan is disconnected on-screen from the market/competitor analysis it was derived from — no 'this plan reflects your competitive market' thread.

items.intelligence: run_id — telemetry / traceability id for the plan
items.gap: Never shown (correctly — it's plumbing). Noted for completeness; no business-story loss.

items.intelligence: objectives[] beyond the first — the full funnel of objectives with their budget split
items.computed_where: media_plan/schemas.py:255 MediaPlan.objectives (List, min 1); both cards hard-index [0] at build.py:385 + server.py:538
items.gap: Both renderers take objectives[0] and silently drop the rest. The schema was explicitly designed for a multi-stage funnel with a real budget split across objectives (schemas.py:8-9), but the dashboard can only ever tell a single-objective story. The moment U1 emits a real 2-3 objective funnel, the owner sees only the first and the whole 'spend 60% here, 40% there' narrative vanishes.

items.intelligence: Comparative Gap Matrix — the full you-vs-peer table of 11 dimensions (online_booking, whatsapp, shows_reviews, cta_count, offerings_count, bilingual, trust_count, social_count, rating, review_count, price_tier) with per-cell values and an ahead/behind/par/whitespace verdict
items.gap: The matrix is the core competitive deliverable, but full_run.py:315 result_doc persists only the SWOT derived from it — the owner never sees the actual side-by-side table (You: booking=yes, rating=4.6 vs Peer A / Peer B). They get bullet prose but not the receipts that make 'you're behind on CTAs' visual and defensible.

items.intelligence: MarketDefinition — geo (country/city/districts/radius_km), category, sub_services, audience sketch, tier, and the bilingual query_seeds actually used to search for peers
items.gap: Computed on every run to widen retrieval and referenced by MediaPlan.market_definition_ref, but never written to result.json and never rendered. The 'here is the market we scoped for you — Egypt / Cairo / Nasr City, these sub-services, this tier, searched with these exact queries' story is invisible, so discovery looks like a black box.

items.intelligence: PeerFitBreakdown — the per-dimension sub-scores (sub_vertical, proximity, size_similarity, audience_tier, language) and the weights_used that produced each peer_fit_score
items.gap: _competitor_card (build.py:94) renders only the total as an 'X% peer fit' number. The owner sees a score with zero explanation of WHY a business is a peer (same sub-vertical? nearby? similar size?), so the match cannot be trusted or defended in a client meeting.

items.intelligence: peer_fit_score rendered as 'peer fit %' — but for web/SERP-discovered peers it is literally 1.0/organic_rank, not the 5-dimension match
items.gap: Both sample runs (nti reach, rawafrican ecommerce) use the web engine, so the rank-1 peer shows '100% peer fit' — which only means 'appeared first on Google', not 'a near-identical competitor'. The label overstates rigor and misleads a non-marketer into thinking a deep similarity match happened.

items.intelligence: why_selected — the provenance string explaining why each competitor was chosen
items.gap: Places peers show 'type=doctor · tier=mid · reviews=180 (2.3x yours) · dist=1.2km · fit=0.72'; web peers show "web search peer (rank 1) for query: 'natural beauty products online'". Both are engineer telemetry, not a business sentence ('A nearby clinic your size that also does laser'). The owner can't read the selection rationale.

items.intelligence: SWOT evidence — the underlying detail/quote behind each S/W/O/T point (SWOTItem.evidence)
items.computed_where: competitor/swot.py:42 SWOTItem.evidence (rendered build.py:77 only as fallback)
items.gap: The task's central question: evidence quotes are NOT shown on hover/expand. _swot_item shows the claim + a source LABEL ('your profile · value_propositions') but never the actual scraped text or the verbatim peer-review quote. Only own-brand review themes leak quotes via the separate Customer-voice section (build.py:340); peer-theme and gap evidence stay hidden, so most SWOT points can't be drilled into for proof.

items.intelligence: claim_strength epistemic ladder — validated / directional_not_validated / internally_supported
items.gap: Rendered as bare badges 'Validated / Directional / Internal' with no legend. A business owner has no idea that 'Directional' means 'only one peer backs this' or 'Internal' means 'from your own site, not peer-validated'. The honesty signal exists but reads as unexplained jargon.

items.intelligence: TOWS strategy type — SO / ST / WO / WT (strength-opportunity, strength-threat, weakness-opportunity, weakness-threat pairings)
items.gap: The two-letter TOWS codes are shown as colored badges with no translation. A non-marketer doesn't know 'SO' = 'use a strength to grab an opportunity'. The build.py:109 _TYPE_TITLES map ('Leverage/Defend/Improve/Protect') exists but the human word isn't surfaced next to the code.

items.intelligence: Strategic posture — leverage / defense / improvement / contingency / balanced
items.gap: Shown as '◎ Strategic posture: leverage' — a single unexplained enum word. It's actually a valuable one-line verdict ('your best move right now is to press your advantages'), but as a raw token it means nothing to the owner and reads as filler.

items.intelligence: TOWS anchors — the SWOT item ids (S1/O2/W1/T1) each strategy and priority action is built from
items.gap: The whole grounding promise of TOWS is 'this strategy traces to Strength-1 + Opportunity-2'. Anchors are computed and valid-by-construction but never rendered or cross-linked to the SWOT quadrants, so the owner can't see which strength/threat a recommended move comes from — the traceability is lost at the last mile.

items.intelligence: priority_actions — rank / action / horizon / anchors / rationale ranked execution plan
items.gap: Now rendered (rank + action + rationale), but horizon is a raw enum 'now/next/later' with no visual timeline, anchors are dropped, and the 'action' text just repeats the strategy title (prefixed 'Leverage:/Improve:'). It reads as a restated list, not a sequenced do-this-first plan a business owner can execute.

items.intelligence: pricing_posture tier signal (extracted = 'mid' for both subjects) — the genuine price-tier of the business
items.gap: TIER-SIGNAL FLAW: pricing_posture is extracted and mapped into MarketDefinition.tier, but discovery.build_match_criteria (discovery.py:82) feeds the peer-fit tier dimension from audience_type (a B2C/B2B/mixed axis) instead — and _normalize_tier('mixed'/'B2C') returns None. So the real price-tier signal never filters or scores peers, and it's never shown. A budget brand can be benchmarked against premium peers with no tier guardrail.

items.intelligence: Places price_level / price_tier per competitor (budget/mid/premium from priceLevel enum)
items.gap: TIER-SIGNAL FLAW: price_tier is defined as an 'info' dimension (direction='info', matrix.py:244) so it never yields a gap verdict and never reaches the SWOT; score_audience_tier only fires when audience_confidence>=0.55 (peer_match.py:56). On the web path (both sample runs) price_level is None entirely. So competitor price positioning — a first-thing-an-owner-asks signal — is computed but neither used for selection nor shown.

items.intelligence: Competitor size / presence-scale — approximated only by Google review_count via size_similarity
items.gap: There is no real branch-count / number-of-locations / presence-scale signal anywhere; 'how big is this rival vs me' is proxied by review volume alone, and even that only appears buried in the why_selected jargon string ('reviews=180 (2.3x yours)'). For web peers, review_count is None so size is unknown and unsurfaced. The owner gets no read on whether a peer is a corner shop or a chain.

items.intelligence: Discovered competitor set + resulting SWOT/TOWS — rebuilt from LIVE search on every run
items.computed_where: competitor/discovery.py:230 client.search_text / web_discovery.py:394 provider.search (no cache/pin in discover_competitors, discovery.py:181)
items.gap: DETERMINISM FLAW (owner-caught): peers come from live Places/SERP queries plus a stochastic LLM query-planner (web_discovery.py:304) and reject-only LLM judge (web_discovery.py:406). Nothing caches or pins the peer set, so re-running the same URL can return different competitors — and therefore a different SWOT and TOWS. A paid deliverable that changes between runs isn't defensible, and the report never discloses the peer set is non-reproducible.

items.intelligence: proximity / distance_m — haversine distance and the radius hard-cap driving local peer selection
items.gap: Distance only ever appears inside the why_selected telemetry string ('dist=1.2km') and is None for the web path. There's no 'peers within X km of your Nasr City branch' map or statement, so the owner can't see the geographic scope the analysis actually used.

items.intelligence: discovery_notes — the audit trail of business_type routing, engine chosen, thin-tier warnings, and candidates considered/passed
items.gap: Notes like 'business_type=ecommerce -> web engine serp-web: 3 web peer(s)' and thin-tier warnings are stored in result.json but the dashboard never renders them. When only 3 of a target 4 peers were found, or the analysis fell back to a web engine, the owner is never told the confidence caveat behind the numbers.

items.intelligence: TowsStrategy.source (rules / llm / llm_text_replaced) and per-strategy claim_strength
items.gap: Each strategy records whether its text is a deterministic template, LLM-crafted, or was swapped back after failing the Evidence Ledger — and its weakest-anchor claim strength. None of this is shown, so unlike SWOT items the strategies carry no visible trust marker; the owner can't tell a validated move from a directional one.

items.intelligence: ABSA own-brand review themes (aspect + polarity + >=2-row support + verbatim quotes) — the whole 'صوت العملاء / Customer voice' deliverable, built with a substring-rejection grounding gate.
items.computed_where: reviews/absa.py:100 extract_aspect_themes + :149 themes_for_swot; wired at competitor/full_run.py:142 _own_voice_themes / :280; rendered dashboard/build.py:337-356
items.gap: The section only renders when a saved review/social file matches the subject's domain slug (full_run.py:121 _voice_files_for). Every REAL deliverable has none — all 7 outputs/*_result.json contain 0 customer-voice SWOT items, and outputs/nti_sci_eg_dashboard.html has no voice section at all. The one capability the owner was told 'must SHOW' (2026-07-12) is invisible in every real client run; it works only on the alameda_hc fixture. No dashboard line tells the owner reviews were never collected.

items.intelligence: SWOT honesty notes / 'what we don't know' caveats: standalone label ('No Competitors Found'), 'competitor comparison too thin', 'Opportunities/Threats need market comparison; supply competitors or a review-theme source', 'own-site items added where the peer comparison had no signal', 'all cells UNKNOWN'.
items.computed_where: competitor/swot.py:181,197-201,220-222,268 (swot.notes); serialized into result.json; dashboard/build.py never reads swot.get('notes')
items.gap: This IS the pipeline's 'what we don't know yet' channel, and the dashboard drops it entirely. marasimltd and iti_gov_eg run in STANDALONE mode with notes ['No Competitors Found', 'O/T need market comparison...'] — yet the client sees a full-looking 4-quadrant SWOT with a KPI reading 'every one cited', with no hint that no competitors were found or that O/T are unpopulated because the comparison failed. The dashboard hides the failure and presents thin analysis as complete.

items.intelligence: Competitor live-ad presence: active_count, longest_days, proven_winners (ads running >=60 days = the market's own split-test winners), plus format and platform priors — deterministic ad-presence math the pitch calls a core insight.
items.computed_where: ads_intel/schemas.py:43 ad_presence + :26 AdPresence; provider ads_intel/providers/meta_ad_library.py; pull scripts/pull_meta_ads.py
items.gap: ad_presence() is called nowhere in the pipeline (only schemas/__init__/tests). It is not wired into full_run, the SWOT, the media plan (media_plan/ has no ads_intel import), or either dashboard. A business owner never learns which competitor ads have been running for months (proven winners) or on which platforms — the single most actionable 'copy what already works' signal is computed-capable but 100% unsurfaced. ads_intel/ has zero fixtures, so even the demo path is empty.

items.intelligence: Ad-intelligence availability gap — the fact that competitor ad presence is BLOCKED pending the owner's META_ADS_TOKEN (the official Ad Library door).
items.computed_where: scripts/pull_meta_ads.py:32-34 (refuses with a stderr print when META_ADS_TOKEN unset)
items.gap: The blocked state lives only as a print in a manual pull script. The dashboard never says 'competitor ad presence: not yet available — connect a Meta token.' The owner cannot tell the difference between 'competitors run no ads' and 'we never looked.' A paid deliverable should name this as a known, closable gap, not stay silent.

items.intelligence: The 'no customer voice collected yet' advisor flag — every review/social provider documents 'empty is VALID -> advisor flag' as the honest signal when no reviews/comments exist.
items.gap: The 'advisor flag' is only a code comment — no code ever constructs, records, or renders such a flag (grep for a gap object across competitor/dashboard/reviews/social_intel/ads_intel/api returns nothing; market_definition.py:7 'advisor flags gaps downstream' is equally aspirational). _own_voice_themes returns [] silently. There is no 'what we don't know yet' panel anywhere in build.py. The dashboard shows only present/positive data and never states an absence.

items.intelligence: The review-theme label a customer complaint/praise is filed under (the aspect), e.g. service quality, waiting time, staff, doctor competence — the human-readable topic of each customer-voice row.
items.computed_where: reviews/absa.py:141 text=f"{labels_ar.get(aspect)} ({aspect})"; taxonomy reviews/taxonomy.py; shown as the bold theme in dashboard/build.py:353
items.gap: The customer-voice row's headline is rendered verbatim as 'جودة الخدمة (service_quality)' — an Arabic label with the raw English enum key bolted on in parentheses. A non-marketer reads a database key, not a sentence. It should read as a story ('Customers consistently praise your service quality — here's what they said'), not 'service_quality'.

items.intelligence: Peer PRAISE themes across competitors ('Category strength to match: X') — recurring things customers love about rivals, i.e. the bar the owner must clear.
items.gap: Peer complaints route into visible SWOT Threats/Opportunities, but peer PRAISE is dumped into swot.notes — which build.py never renders. The owner never sees 'competitors are loved for fast delivery — match it,' even though the pipeline extracted and grounded it. Half of the competitive customer-voice signal is silently discarded.

items.intelligence: Verbatim customer quotes — the grounding receipts that make each theme defensible (the moat: quote is a literal substring of a real review).
items.computed_where: reviews/absa.py:159-160 support=[f"{voice} voice {rid}: «{q[:80]}»"]; rendered as citation lines dashboard/build.py:350-351
items.gap: The quote is prefixed with pipeline jargon ('own voice V3: «...»') and truncated to 80 chars. The receipt that should read as a clean pull-quote from a customer is decorated with an internal row id and voice-mode tag. Strong evidence is there but presented as a debug string, weakening the demo it was built for.

items.intelligence: Social signals — Instagram/Facebook captions + customer comments (own brand) and competitor public captions (peer marketing voice / content intelligence), privacy-hashed at ingestion.
items.gap: Social signals have no dashboard section. They only enter the product if a social fixture happens to match the subject slug and then fold anonymously into ABSA own-voice (full_run.py:130) — no real subject has one. Peer captions (the 'competitor marketing voice' the module was built to expose) are never surfaced anywhere. The whole U9 social door is dark in the deliverable.

items.intelligence: Customer-voice polarity (praise vs complaint) and support strength (how many distinct customers said it) per theme.
items.gap: In the Customer-voice card, praise vs complaint is conveyed ONLY by an emoji + background color (💬 sage vs ⚠ gold) with no words, and the support count ('3 customers raised this') is not shown at all. A non-marketer scanning the card cannot tell strength or even reliably read the sentiment; the honesty of 'how many customers' is computed but dropped.

items.intelligence: Social-pull budget governance — the Apify $20/month spend cap and whether a social pull was skipped because it would exceed budget.
items.gap: The guard can REFUSE a pull and explain why, but that refusal is internal to the pull path. If social voice is thin because the budget cap blocked collection, the owner is never told 'we stopped at the $20 cap' — it looks identical to 'no social data exists.' A budget-driven data gap reads as an information gap.

items.intelligence: Claim-strength / epistemic honesty ladder — validated (>=2 peers), directional_not_validated (single-peer/single-theme), internally_supported (own-site only) — computed deterministically, never by the LLM.
items.computed_where: competitor/swot.py:308 _gap_strength, :156 theme_strength; rendered dashboard/build.py:70-81 as a badge
items.gap: This is the positive control: honesty that IS told well — every SWOT line carries a Validated / Directional / Internal badge, so the owner sees how sure each claim is. The same badge treatment should be extended to the currently-hidden signals above (voice availability, standalone caveats, ad-presence status) so the dashboard's honesty is consistent rather than selective.

items.intelligence: On-topic market TRENDS matched to the brand (trend title + matched_terms) mapped into SWOT Opportunities/Threats, e.g. 'Rising interest in beauty, care: The Biggest Skin-Care Trends of 2026', cited to the trend URL, tagged claim_strength=directional_not_validated
items.computed_where: competitor/brand_signals.py:161 opportunities_threats_from_trends (wired at competitor/full_run.py:288-299); rendered dashboard/build.py:76 _swot_item
items.gap: These live, time-sensitive trend signals are folded anonymously into the SWOT grid and shown only as a 'Directional' badge + a bare URL. A business owner cannot tell these are CURRENT trends to ride NOW (vs. static analysis) — the 'trend' framing, the recency, and the call-to-act are all lost. This is the owner's 'trends run but are never shown' finding: there is no Trends section anywhere on the dashboard.

items.intelligence: Trend RANKING: per-source normalized popularity + recency-decay -> trend_score (0..1), on-topic-first ordering, and the matched business keywords per trend (matched_terms)
items.gap: The engine that decides WHICH trends matter and how fresh/hot each is (the whole value of a trend feed) never reaches the client. The owner sees no 'what's hot in your category this month, ranked' view — only the leftover titles buried in SWOT. No dashboard code reads trend_score.

items.intelligence: Calendar TREND ATTRIBUTION per content item (which post rides which current trend) — the builder explicitly feeds trend titles to the planner with 'RIDE THESE CURRENT TRENDS where they fit'
items.gap: Two-layer miss: (1) ContentItem has NO trend field, so even when trends are supplied the output item records nothing about the trend it rode; (2) the dashboard's own analyze() calls strategy WITHOUT --trends (dashboard/run.py:116), so in the live product the calendar never rides trends at all. Verified: outputs/nti_sci_eg_plan.json and rawafrican_net_plan.json items contain zero 'trend' references. The owner gets bare date/platform/type/topic/hook rows with no reason WHY a post is timed now.

items.intelligence: Per-run LLM COST (cost_usd), tokens_in/tokens_out, and model per pipeline stage — real values recorded, e.g. cost_usd=0.110554, tokens_in=40259, tokens_out=6023, model=gemini-2.5-pro
items.computed_where: telemetry/logger.py:94-95 (RunTelemetry.record cost_usd); produced at business_profile/build.py:206; persisted to runs/<run_id>/telemetry.jsonl
items.gap: TELEMETRY COST HIDDEN: 20 runs on disk each carry a real per-run cost (~$0.11) + token counts + model, but neither dashboard/build.py nor dashboard/server.py ever reads runs/. A paying client (or the owner pricing the deliverable) sees zero cost/spend/token accounting — the unit economics of the campaign are computed and thrown away.

items.intelligence: Per-stage RUN TELEMETRY: latency_ms, status (ok/error), and decisions (e.g. decision='rejections=2', note='dropped_fields=1') for each stage-call (rules, evidence_pack, llm_extraction, validate, merge)
items.computed_where: telemetry/logger.py:72 RunTelemetry.record; runs/<run_id>/telemetry.jsonl (100 lines across 20 runs)
items.gap: The audit trail of WHAT the pipeline did and how long it took (the reproducibility/quality evidence) is invisible on the dashboard. The QA strip that IS shown (dashboard/build.py:443-460) reports only scrape duration from a separate scrape manifest — none of the telemetry latency/decision/rejection data reaches the client.

items.intelligence: Content-calendar BRAND-SAFETY AUDIT: gate_active, evidence_count (120), items_total, items_remediated (1 hook blanked), and a per-item (claim -> real source URL) shipped-copy trail + remediation log
items.gap: The audit sidecar exists for every brand (nti_sci_eg_plan.audit.json shows 1 item remediated, 120 evidence entries) but the dashboard never reads *_plan.audit.json. The calendar section shows a static 'grounding-gated hooks' caption (dashboard/build.py:491) with no receipts. items.gap: The dashboard headlines a 'Provable Brand Safety' pill (dashboard/build.py:525) yet never renders the actual proof: real sheets on disk (e.g. verdict=PASS, 1 claim verified, 2 remediated) are ignored — the dashboard has zero references to .compliance.json. The single most sellable artifact ('here is the signed compliance sheet an agency hands its client') is computed and never shown.

items.intelligence: EGYPTIAN-SEASON WINDOW (Ramadan / Eid / back-to-school / local retail seasons) to time calendar posts and creative to the buying calendar
items.computed_where: nowhere — absent (only a 'eid-offer' string in a product-name prettifier docstring, dashboard/products.py:27); calendar dates are a blind even-spread over N days (strategy/builder.py:180-197)
items.gap: No Egyptian-season logic is computed at all. The 14/30-day calendar spaces posts mechanically and the trend engine is date-agnostic (recency decay, not calendar seasons), so an EG business gets no Ramadan/Eid/back-to-school timing — the single highest-leverage local marketing signal. The story a paying EG owner expects ('post THIS before Eid') cannot be told because the pipeline never derives the window.

items.intelligence: Per calendar-item REMEDIATION record: a fabricated hook/angle that the grounding gate blanked, with the original text, the unsourced claim kinds, and the 'runs on its sourced topic' note
items.gap: The remediation array lives in every plan.json item, but the dashboard's _calendar_row (dashboard/build.py:120) reads only date/platform/topic/hook and drops it. A hook that was blanked for fabrication just renders as an empty hook with no explanation — the owner sees a thinner post, not the 'we caught and removed a false claim here' safety story.

items.intelligence: Rubric A — first-screen story / executive summary
items.gap: There is NO executive summary. The first screen is a Baseera product pitch ('{name} — a complete campaign, from one URL', line 528) plus a generic fallback tagline, followed by 5 KPI tiles that are INVENTORY COUNTS (offerings=7, competitors=4, SWOT=18, value-props=5, calendar posts). A business owner opens to 'how many things we counted', never 'here is your situation and the 3 things to do'. No situation→insight→recommendation. FAIL.

items.intelligence: Rubric B — plan-not-enum (media plan decoded to human language)
items.gap: The EXPORTED media plan decodes enums well (OUTCOME_LEADS→'عملاء محتملون · Leads', lead_form→'نموذج تواصل', bofu→'تحويل · BOFU'). But the STUDIO's own Arabic card leaks raw internals for the SAME plan: funnel prints '(funnel_stage).upper()'='BOFU' (server.py:564) and KPI prints kpi.metric='cost_per_lead' (server.py:566). Inconsistent: the two deliverables decode the same object differently. PARTIAL PASS / studio FAIL.

items.intelligence: Rubric C — strategy narrative (TOWS + posture as prose)
items.gap: TOWS renders as machine-templated strings: unexplained acronym badges SO/ST/WO/WT and auto-concatenated 'Leverage: {strength} — {opportunity}' sentences (result.json strategies). Posture prints as a single raw word: '◎ Strategic posture: leverage' (build.py:483). Priority actions repeat the identical 'Leverage:…' templates with horizon 'now'. No human explains WHAT the strategy is or WHY. A non-marketer cannot parse SO/ST/WO/WT or 'leverage'. FAIL.

items.intelligence: Rubric D — creative tied to strategy/audience/funnel
items.gap: The reel pipeline computes a full narrative — concept ('young Egyptian graduate's journey…HireReady program, land a job in 4 months'), hook, music_mood, cta 'Apply now', scene list — but NONE of it is shown. The creative section is a bare poster+video plus boilerplate ('Every hard claim traces to real evidence'). Creatives are ORPHANED: not labeled with which objective (Leads/BOFU), which audience segment, or which calendar item they serve. FAIL.

items.intelligence: Rubric E — voice of customer
items.gap: For these real artifacts the section DOES NOT RENDER: NTI has 0 own-brand 'customer voice' SWOT items and all 4 competitors have reviews:[] (0). The block only appears if SWOT evidence contains the literal string 'customer voice', so it silently vanishes with no honest 'no reviews found for this brand' state. Competitor reviews are collected in the schema but empty and unused. FAIL for this deliverable.

items.intelligence: Rubric F — honesty surface (Evidence-Ledger audit + remediation)
items.computed_where: outputs/nti_sci_eg_plan.audit.json (gate_active, coverage, evidence_count, items_remediated) — never read by build.py/server.py
items.gap: The audit proves the moat: the 2026-07-25 calendar hook was BLANKED for a fabricated 'first' claim (plan.json remediation). The dashboard never shows the audit; worse, the blanked hook renders as EMPTY (build.py:131 suppresses empty quotes) so the honesty action looks like a missing hook. claim_strength badges on SWOT (validated/directional/internal, build.py:70-83) and the media-plan '✓ مؤكد بالأدلة' are the only honesty signals; the actual remediation log and coverage are invisible. FAIL.

items.intelligence: Rubric G — zero raw internals
items.gap: Multiple internals leak to the client: SWOT citations print '↳ your profile · value_propositions' and 'readiness.swot_quality_signals.tagline=false' (raw model.field); a weakness reads 'Your number of ctas (3) is below the peer average (5.8, n=4)' (jargon 'ctas', 'n=4'); the count line shows swot mode 'competitive'; TOWS SO/ST/WO/WT + posture 'leverage'; the studio Arabic card leaks 'BOFU'/'cost_per_lead'; and the 'Data coverage' panel exposes scraper telemetry — pages_attempted, 'text blocks', 'failures', per-page block counts. FAIL.

items.intelligence: Rubric H — five-minute ordered read
items.gap: No guided arc, no section numbers, no 'start here'. Export order: hero→KPIs→SWOT→[voice]→MEDIA PLAN→competitors→TOWS→priority actions→calendar→creative→DATA COVERAGE last. The buying plan sits before competitors, and the deliverable ENDS on scraper internals ('Data coverage'). The studio reorders entirely — Arabic media-plan card FIRST, then SWOT — so the two deliverables tell the story in different sequences. No narrative path (situation→evidence→strategy→plan→creative→proof). FAIL.

items.intelligence: RTL / bilingual handling for an Arabic-market deliverable
items.computed_where: build.py:539 (<html lang="en">) + server.py:61,618; no dir=rtl anywhere except dir=auto on HITL inputs (server.py:606,610)
items.gap: The exported dashboard is wrapped <html lang="en"> with NO dir=rtl, no mirrored layout, and no Arabic font stack — yet nearly all CONTENT is Arabic (calendar topics/hooks, TOWS descriptions, media-plan labels). Arabic renders LTR-aligned inside English-labeled containers. Section headings (SWOT, Competitors, TOWS, Content calendar, KPI labels) are English-only; only the media-plan and voice headers are bilingual. For an Egyptian client this reads as a half-localized draft, not an agency deliverable.

items.intelligence: Design/type quality bar vs an agency deliverable
items.computed_where: build.py:145-146 (--serif Fraunces/--sans Inter), :101/server.py Space Grotesk; no @font-face or <link> in either file
items.gap: Fraunces, Inter and Space Grotesk are NAMED in the CSS but never loaded (no web-font @font-face/link — confirmed absent), so the 'elegant serif display' silently falls back to Georgia/system sans on any machine without them; the intended type system is not actually delivered. Palette (blush/sand/sage/gold) is cohesive and the rounded-card layout is polished, but it reads as a generic SaaS dashboard template, not a bespoke brand deliverable; combined with the RTL gaps and raw-internal leaks it sits below the agency bar it claims ('agency-grade').

items.intelligence: 7 real offerings + 5 value propositions (the actual selling lines)
items.computed_where: profile.offerings (7) / profile.value_propositions (5); build.py:307-308,319,322 use ONLY len()
items.gap: Both are rendered ONLY as KPI COUNTS ('7 Offerings', '5 Value props'). The actual offerings list is never printed, and the value props ('Bridges the talent-industry gap…', 'practical training on multinational-grade simulation networks…') surface only indirectly as SWOT strengths. The owner's core catalog and strongest selling lines — the heart of what they sell — are reduced to two numbers on the first screen.

items.intelligence: 8 trust signals (accreditations, certifications, partnerships)
items.computed_where: profile.trust_signals (8 items) — never referenced in build.py/server.py
items.gap: Fully dropped. For a training institute this is the credibility spine: 'Accredited by the Supreme Council of Universities', ITU 10-year certificate, Cisco CCNA / VMware VCP / ISO 27001 training, named partnerships. None appears anywhere on the dashboard. The single most persuasive, client-usable proof set is computed and thrown away.

items.computed_where: profile.audience_signals (5), profile.pricing_posture ('mid'), profile.service_areas (Egypt/Cairo/Nasr City/Smart Village/Alexandria) — unused by the dashboard

The dashboard shows none of them; the media plan only surfaces a vague 'audience: mixed' and geo 'national', discarding the specific who/where a media buyer actually needs.
